_comment: Phase 3 depth and light. Level id -> which backdrop world it uses, how much air is in front of that backdrop, how far each tile layer is knocked back, and where the lights are. levels/*.json is geometry only and did not change for this phase; this is the mood, kept apart from it so an artist can re-light the game without touching a single tile.

_fields.air: haze quad drawn over the parallax and behind the tiles: ramp step + alpha
_fields.bg_tint: multiplier on the background tile layer: ramp step for the hue, mix for how much of that hue, scale for how far back it sits
_fields.fg_tint: the same for the solid layer. Keep it near 1.0 - this is what the player reads as ground
_fields.vignette: 0..1 strength of the screen-edge darkening, drawn over the tiles and under the entities
_fields.lights: additive pools at tile coordinates. radius in px, intensity 0..1, flicker 0..1
_fields.emissive: tile id -> a pool on every one of those tiles, merged along a row

_colours: Every ramp/step pair indexes assets/palette.json, which tools/art/palette.py generates. No RGB literals: an ambient tint multiplies the whole screen, so it has to come off the same ramps as the art.

jungle_1._note: CANOPY TRAIL. Daylight. The backdrop does the work; the air is only thick enough to keep the far trees behind the tiles.

jungle_2._note: ROOT HOLLOW. The dark one. Its bg layer is a solid wall of bg_rock on every screen, so the parallax is never visible here - all of the depth is tint, vignette and the lights that pick out the route.

jungle_3._note: THE WATERWAY. Also walled in bg_rock, so again no parallax. The water surface lights itself: every run of water_top gets one pool.

jungle_4._note: SKY BRANCH. The bright one. The haze is pale rather than dark, which is the whole trick: it lifts the backdrop towards the sky instead of pushing it towards black.

jungle_5._note: HEART OF THE GROVE. The boss arena: same jungle backdrop as CANOPY TRAIL, pushed violet so the last level does not look like the first one.

ruins_1._note: DROWNED STEPS. The first of the sunken world, so it is the one that has to *introduce* it: the ruins backdrop - a drowned colonnade going blue with distance - is left as readable as it ever gets here, and the haze is only thick enough to sit the stone behind the tiles.

ruins_2._note: THE COLONNADE. The level is a colonnade and so is the backdrop, so this is the one screen in the game where the parallax and the tiles are the same architecture receding. The tint keeps them apart by value rather than by hue.

ruins_3._note: TIDE GALLERY. Half the level is under water and the currents run through it, so the surface does the lighting: every run of water_top gets its own pool, exactly as THE WATERWAY does.

ruins_4._note: THE CISTERN. Enclosed and flooded - the darkest of the five. The haze is nearly black water and the vignette closes the walls in; the only thing that gives light back is the surface itself.

ruins_5._note: THE TIDE MAW. The arena floods and drains under the player, so the light has to move with it: the pools are on the water surface, not on the walls, and they rise and fall with the tide because the tile they are attached to does.

heights_1._note: UPDRAFT. First screen of world 3 and the one that has to sell the altitude, so it gets the least air of the five: the heights backdrop - a dusk sky over snow peaks standing out of a sea of cloud - is meant to be looked at here.

heights_2._note: THE THERMALS. The vents are what lift you, so they are the only thing in the level that emits: a low ember pool on every heights_vent, merged along a row, which reads as heat coming off the rock rather than as a lamp.

heights_3._note: ASH COLUMN. The dim one: ash in the air rather than haze, so the backdrop is pushed towards the ember ramp instead of towards black and the peaks go the colour of the sky.

heights_4._note: THE LONG GLIDE. The brightest screen in the game. Eleven hundred cloud tiles, almost no vignette and the palest haze there is: nothing here should read as a ceiling.

heights_5._note: THE STORMCREST. Same peaks as the other four, under weather. The air goes stone grey and the vignette closes in, which is what makes the bird - drawn on the stone ramp itself - read by silhouette instead of by colour.

test_arena._note: Left neutral on purpose. tools/itest.sh plays here, and a test that has to be re-baselined every time someone re-lights a level is a test nobody trusts.
